name: Doha
title: Doha Ship Thickness Measurement | Hamad Port & Mesaieed
description: UTM at Hamad Port, Mesaieed and offshore bases: ship thickness measurement in Doha covering hull structure, renewal survey and pre-docking gauging.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ships at Hamad Port and Doha
intro: Hamad Port, south of Doha, is Qatar's main gateway for containers, vehicles and general cargo, and nearby Mesaieed serves the country's petrochemical, fertiliser and steel industries. Offshore, a sizeable support fleet works Qatar's oil and gas fields. We carry out ship thickness measurement in Doha and across Qatar for renewal surveys, pre-docking steel estimates and condition gauging, and the team comes over from India to work on board, whether the ship is at a berth or at anchor.

highlights.p: Bulk carriers in Mesaieed's fertiliser trade suffer hold corrosion when hygroscopic cargo residues pick up moisture. Targeted gauging at frame brackets, hopper plating and tank tops finds the pitting that general readings can miss.
Container ships, car carriers and multipurpose ships at Hamad Port can release piping, decks and selected ballast tanks during a call. Those readings feed the full programme at the next docking.

Supply boats, crew boats and anchor handlers serving Qatar's fields come into port between contracts. That idle time is the practical window for renewal gauging and for the condition record a new charterer expects.

port.h: Doha, Hamad Port and Qatar's working waterfront
p: Qatar moved its container and general cargo trade out of the old Doha port when Hamad Port opened south of the capital, and the old port in the city now concentrates on cruise ships. Hamad Port, managed by Mwani Qatar with its container terminals run by QTerminals, handles mainline and feeder container services, vehicle carriers, general cargo and project cargo. Further south, Mesaieed is the industrial port, loading petrochemicals, fertilisers, steel and refined products and receiving raw materials for the industrial city that surrounds it.

Several things keep ships in Qatari waters long enough to gauge. Car carriers and multipurpose ships can spend a day or more alongside at Hamad Port, bulk carriers loading fertiliser or steel at Mesaieed can spend several days at the berth or waiting at anchorage, and the offshore support vessels serving Qatar's fields come into Doha, Mesaieed and Ras Laffan between charters or for surveys. Qatar's position as an LNG exporter also brings a steady flow of gas carriers and of tankers lifting condensate and products, most of which load in the north at Ras Laffan rather than near the capital. In the winter season, cruise ships turning round at the old Doha port add a short window for piping checks close to the city centre.

What drives inspection work around Doha is the country's mix of industries. Fertiliser cargoes are hard on holds; product and chemical tankers loading at Mesaieed come under strict charterer vetting; and the offshore fleet works in warm, shallow water around platforms and pipelines. Owners also look ahead. The expansion of Qatar's LNG production is drawing new ships, supply vessels and support craft into the country's waters, and charterers can ask for recent gauging records before they accept a vessel. A ship manager in Doha is therefore as likely to want gauging for a commercial decision as for a class survey, and the two are often combined in one visit.

facilities.h: Where thickness gauging happens around Doha
p: Thickness gauging at Hamad Port is done alongside during a ship's call or while it waits at the port's anchorage, usually as a limited scope, such as piping, deck plating, hatch coamings or a sample of ballast tanks, fitted around cargo work. Full renewal-survey programmes need a dry dock, and Qatar's large-ship docking is done at the Erhama Bin Jaber Al Jalahma Shipyard at Ras Laffan in the north, so many Doha-managed ships combine pre-docking readings at Hamad Port with the full programme at the yard.

Hull gauging at Mesaieed covers bulk carriers, product and chemical tankers and the industrial port's tugs and service craft, either alongside when the terminal allows or at anchorage. Offshore vessel gauging in Qatar happens at the supply bases and repair berths serving the offshore fields, where supply boats, crew boats and anchor handlers come in for maintenance between charters. Because Hamad Port, Mesaieed and the offshore bases are all within driving distance of Doha, a team in the country for one ship can usually take on a second without a new mobilisation, provided the port passes are in place.
list: Hamad Port container and general cargo berths — piping, deck and hold gauging on boxships, car carriers and multipurpose tonnage during their calls
Hamad Port anchorage — pre-purchase and on-hire condition checks on vessels queued for a berth, reached by launch booked through the agent
Mesaieed Port — holds, tank tops and ballast tanks of bulk carriers loading fertiliser and steel, plus condition gauging on product and chemical tankers
Doha Port — sea water and fire main lines, plus exhaust gas cleaning wash-water piping where fitted, on cruise ships turning round in the winter season
Offshore supply bases and repair berths — renewal-survey gauging on supply vessels, crew boats and anchor handlers serving Qatar's offshore fields
Erhama Bin Jaber Al Jalahma Shipyard, Ras Laffan — full renewal-survey programmes for Doha-managed ships when they dock in Qatar

context.h: Regulation and market context for ship inspection in Qatar
p: Port state control in Qatar operates under the Riyadh MoU, so ships calling at Hamad Port, Mesaieed and Ras Laffan are subject to port state control inspections under that regime. The Gulf has no emission control area, which leaves the 0.50% global cap as the applicable sulphur limit; Qatar's ports see both ships running on compliant fuel and scrubber-fitted container ships and bulk carriers. On the latter, wash-water and overboard piping is a corrosion hotspot that can be checked during a normal port call, without waiting for the next docking.

The market is dominated by energy. QatarEnergy's expansion of LNG output from the North Field has driven one of the largest LNG carrier newbuilding programmes ever placed, and the growth of the gas business brings more offshore and support vessels into service around the country. Bulk carriers in Mesaieed's fertiliser trade need particular attention: urea and other fertilisers that pick up moisture attack hold coatings and steel, causing pitting and grooving at frame brackets, hopper plating and tank tops. Summer heat is severe, and Qatar's rules restrict outdoor work during the hottest hours of the summer months, so gauging plans have to build in those limits from the start rather than absorb them as delays.

jobs.h: Common gauging scopes in Doha and across Qatar
jobs.p: Most enquiries for ultrasonic thickness measurement in Qatar fall into three groups: deep-sea ships calling at Hamad Port or Mesaieed, offshore vessels between charters, and ships preparing for a docking at Ras Laffan. The scenarios below are typical, and each is scoped from the survey status, the vessel's gauging history and the time it will spend alongside or at anchor.
list: Hold and tank-top gauging on a Supramax bulk carrier loading urea at Mesaieed, focusing on frame brackets, lower hopper plating and the double-bottom ballast tanks below.
Pre-docking readings on a product tanker at Mesaieed anchorage, sent ahead to the Ras Laffan yard before its renewal survey so steel quantities are agreed before docking.
Scrubber piping and seawater line checks on a container ship during a Hamad Port call, including the overboard sections near the shell where wall loss is usually greatest.
Renewal-survey gauging of a crew boat or supply vessel between offshore charters, covering hull, deck, fuel and water tanks and the stern structure.
On-hire condition gauging at Hamad Port of a car carrier entering a period charter, measuring vehicle deck plating, ramps and ballast tanks for an agreed starting record.

logistics: The team flies into Hamad International Airport (DOH), with non-stop services from many Indian cities; the onward journey to Hamad Port, Mesaieed or the offshore bases is by road. Port entry needs ISPS passes and, for some industrial areas, additional security permits, all arranged through the ship's agent; anchorage boarding is by launch booked the same way. Qatar's entry requirements for the team are completed before departure, so we need the ship's ETA or docking date early and confirm the mobilisation once permits are in hand.

faqs.q: Can you carry out gauging alongside at Hamad Port during a normal call?
faqs.a: Limited scopes, yes. Piping, deck plating, hatch coamings, ballast tanks the crew can empty and ventilate, and selected void spaces can be gauged during a call if the master releases them. A full renewal-survey programme needs dry-dock access to the bottom and all tanks, which is why most Doha-managed ships combine port-call readings with a programme at the yard.

faqs.q: Why do fertiliser cargoes from Mesaieed matter for hold gauging?
faqs.a: Urea and other fertilisers are hygroscopic. Moisture from condensation or leaking hatch covers turns residues into a corrosive solution that attacks paint and steel at the bottom of holds, around frame brackets and along hopper plating. Bulk carriers that spend years in this trade can show local pitting and grooving well before general wastage limits are reached, so we target those areas specifically.

faqs.q: Does Qatar's summer heat restrict when gauging can be done?
faqs.a: It shapes the daily plan. Qatar limits outdoor work during the hottest hours of the summer months, and tanks heated by the sun need extra ventilation before entry. We start early, prioritise exposed decks and hatch covers for the cooler hours, and keep enclosed-space work to periods when the atmosphere and temperature are within safe limits for the people inside.

faqs.q: Can one mobilisation cover ships at Hamad Port and Ras Laffan?
faqs.a: Yes, if the schedules allow. Hamad Port, Mesaieed and Ras Laffan are each a drive from Doha, so a team in Qatar for a ship at one can move to another. Ras Laffan has stricter entry controls than the southern ports, so we ask the agent to start that permit application at the same time as the Hamad Port pass, not after the first job finishes.
